t: 3249. Count the Number of Good Nodes
o: Root the tree at node 0; a node is good when all its children's subtree sizes are equal (leaves and nodes with a single child are trivially good). We must count good nodes for n up to 1e5. Compute subtree sizes bottom-up, then test each node's children for equal sizes. In example 1 every node qualifies (7); in example 3 only node 9 fails because its children's subtrees have sizes 3 and 2.
k: Subtree sizes come from one post-order traversal.
A node is good iff the set of its children's sizes has at most one distinct value.
With n up to 1e5, prefer an iterative traversal to avoid recursion-depth crashes on path-shaped trees.

a.i: Build adjacency lists, DFS from the root returning subtree sizes, and count a node as good when all returned child sizes are identical. Clean and short, provided the language's stack can handle the depth (raise Python's recursion limit).
s: DFS(u, parent): collect sizes from all children; recurse and sum.
Mark u good if the collected child sizes are all equal; return 1 + sum of child sizes.
a.t: O(n) — each node and edge is visited once
a.sp: O(n) for adjacency lists plus recursion stack up to O(n)

a.i: Avoid recursion entirely: BFS from the root recording parents and a visit order, derive children lists, initialize every size to 1, then process nodes in reverse BFS order so children are finalized before parents. Compare child sizes per node to count good nodes. Safe for deep path graphs.
s: BFS from node 0 recording parent[] and order[].
Build children[p] lists from parent relationships.
Iterate order reversed: gather children sizes into a set; if at most one distinct size, increment good; then add children sizes into size[u].
a.t: O(n) — BFS plus one reverse pass
a.sp: O(n) for adjacency, order, and size arrays

w: Leaves and single-child nodes are automatically good — make sure your equality check treats empty/single-element sets correctly. The iterative version is the safer interview answer for n = 1e5 path trees. Follow-up: count nodes whose children's sizes differ by at most 1, or report the deepest bad node.
